body_ar: فإذا رأيتم ما تكرهون، أي رأيتم ريحا قد أقبل تكرهونه والرياح العواصف تهدم البيوت في كثير من الأحيان ويتضرر بها الزرع وتؤذِي الناسَ، فإذا رأيتم ما تكرهون أي ما تتوقعون فيه ذلك فقولوا اللهم إنا نسألك من خير هذه الريح وخير ما فيها، وخير ما أمرت به، فهذه ثلاثة أدعية، الدعاء الأول اللهم إنا نسألك من خير هذه الريح، فالريح نفسها قد تأتي بخير وقد تأتي بشر،
body_en: 'So when you see what you find hateful' — that is, when you see a wind coming on that you find hateful. Gale winds often bring houses down; crops are damaged by them and people are harmed. 'So when you see what you find hateful' — that is, what you expect that from — 'then say: O God, we ask You for the good of this wind, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what it has been commanded with' (اللهم إنا نسألك من خير هذه الريح وخير ما فيها وخير ما أمرت به). These are three supplications. The first supplication is 'O God, we ask You for the good of this wind': the wind itself may bring good and may bring evil,

flags.context: The title of the series, appearing in the title of articles 502–516.
options: al-Mughnī al-Mufīd (left untranslated as a work title)
The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: فإذا رأيتم ما تكرهون، أي رأيتم ريحا قد أقبل تكرهونه
flags.note: تكرهون here is the ordinary verb of aversion in a hadith text, NOT the legal category makrūh ('disliked'). 'Dislike' has been avoided in the English so that no reader takes this for a ruling word. Flagged because the corpus fixes 'disliked' for makrūh and the collision is easy to make.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
The supplication is retained in Arabic alongside the English, per the style guide rule for duʿāʾ formulae, since the Arabic is the operative recited text.
The Sheikh gives no narrator or collection for the hadith he is expounding, and none has been supplied.
